answer: An agent economy can price identity so every extra persona an operator claims costs double. Ten fake agents mean a bond worth a thousand units, and a judge who catches collusion burns the entire stack. An operator loosing a falcon of bot personas ends up bankrolling the network he meant to drain. Cedar survives dry country because cutting one grove raises the price of the next, and an oasis holds caravans for the same reason: density built on real collateral stays expensive to fake, so honest agents keep the advantage.
